heroHeadline: Congress ratifies $1.9B IMF deal; Paz eliminates diesel subsidy entirely, price jumps 83% as COB and transport unions threaten blockades
heroSubtitle: The Chamber of Deputies approved the 36-month IMF Extended Fund Facility on Sept. 18 and the Senate sanctioned it via a waived-procedure vote (Law 723) on Sept. 19, completing congressional ratification of the $1.9 billion program first agreed at staff level July 29; final IMF Executive Board approval is expected around Oct. 2. Hours later, President Paz announced in a recorded message the total elimination of the diesel subsidy under Supreme Decree 5716, replacing the two-tier Bs. 9.80/Bs. 18.00 pricing with a single Bs. 17.95-per-liter rate for all consumers effective Sept. 20 — an roughly 83% increase — paired with an expanded PEPE cash bonus for about 2.9 million recipients and Bs. 800 million in preferential transporter credit. The COB rejected the decree and convened an undated national emergency assembly, the Confederación de Choferes declared its own state of emergency and set a national assembly for Monday, Sept. 21, La Paz's interprovincial transport federation announced a departmental blockade starting the same day, and tanker operators (cisterneros) suspended fuel loading indefinitely, while the boliviano weakened to Bs. 11.00/$1 on the central bank's official rate.
footerNote: Data sourced from official reports, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
